subject: Custom SLA addendum & onboarding playbook request
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@medlinkhealth.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: Leah Ortiz <lortiz@medlinkhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 7 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: custom SLA addendum + onboarding playbook

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with Redwood's routing and fallback model variants. Procurement and legal have asked me to formalize a request for a custom SLA addendum to sit alongside our enterprise MSA/SOW and the order form. High level asks:

- Target availability: 99.95% across primary region, with cross-region failover within 5m for leader election events
- Latency objective: P95 < 120ms for generation calls under normal load (single-request profile) and clear documentation for degraded modes
- Scheduled maintenance windows: prefer monthly 1h windows outside 02:00-08:00 PT; need notice >=72h
- Evidence required for procurement: hourly uptime export, per-route latency histograms, last 6 months SOC2 summary, and incident postmortems for Sev1
- Order form language: explicit fallback to lower-capacity model with no credit if customer elects to use degraded model; otherwise, credits for platform-level unavailability

I've attached a short PDF that procurement compiled (MedLink_SLA_Request.pdf) with our suggested redlines. Can you route to your legal and ops teams and let me know what evidence you can provide and how Redwood would handle the fallback / ordered-tiering language in the order form? We'll need an onboarding playbook that maps evidence handoffs and a DocuSign flow.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of Procurement, MedLink Health
(attachment: MedLink_SLA_Request.pdf)

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@medlinkhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 7 May 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: custom SLA addendum + onboarding playbook

Samir —

Appreciate the clear asks and the PDF. I've looped in Karthik (legal/ops lead) and Ben (solutions/procurement) to move this forward. Quick clarifying questions so we scope the addendum correctly:

1) The 99.95% target — is that for request-level availability (HTTP 5xx/timeout) or for a broader service-level (including routing/fallback)?
2) For P95 120ms, can you share a representative sample request size and typical prompt length? It affects kernel selection and compaction paths.
3) Evidence cadence: do you need realtime access to uptime exports (API push) or regular CSV exports?
4) For the fallback language, do you want Redwood to automatically fail to a lower-cost model when capacity is constrained, or do you prefer manual/partner-triggered fallback?

We'll propose draft order-form language and an onboarding checklist: evidence endpoints, who signs off on runbook, canary schedule, and DocuSign path. I'll aim to get a first draft by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

On Thu, May 7, 2026 at 9:12 AM Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@medlinkhealth.com> wrote:
> Hi Vivek,
>
> Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with Redwood's routing and fallback model variants...

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 8 May 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: draft availability rider + onboarding checklist

Vivek / Ben —

I've sketched two short options for order-form wording and an onboarding checklist. Attaching a working draft (availability-rider-draft.docx). Key callouts:

- Option A (preferred for enterprise): Commit to 99.95% regional availability measured at the edge gateway for the "production" route. Scheduled maintenance (monthly, 1h max) excluded; credits apply only when Redwood's platform-class outage impacts customer requests routed to production and not when customer invokes degraded-tier/model choice.

- Option B (stricter): 99.975% with a tiered credit schedule but requires additional reserved capacity (pricing delta).

Onboarding checklist (high level):
- Pre-go-live: legal sign-off on rider, shared SAML config, KMS integration plan, SOC2 artifact bundle
- Canary: 72h canary with traffic ramp and synthetic checks (we'll supply the synthetic harness)
- Evidence handoff: S3 bucket + signed transfer cadence (hourly exports for 30d, daily thereafter) or API push as part of Dedicated/Private package

I've included proposed credit formulas and a sample fallback clause that allows automatic failover to a named lower-capacity model ONLY when Redwood detects capacity exhaustion at the serving tier and after an attempt to route to compatible variant. If MedLink prefers manual toggle, we can remove automation.

(attachment: availability-rider-draft.docx)

—Karthik

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: draft availability rider + onboarding checklist

Adding a few pragmatic notes for procurement and evidence:

- Evidence matrix: customer needs mapping of dataset (hourly uptime, per-route latency percentiles, incident timelines). I've populated a starter (evidence-matrix.xlsx) with the fields MedLink asked for.
- DocuSign flow: we should send the rider as an exhibit to the order form and collect signatures in this order: CSM -> MedLink procurement -> Redwood legal -> Redwood exec signoff. Use DocuSign envelope template RIDER-2026-V1.
- If they insist on automatic cross-region failover within 5m for leader election, that is an operational SLA that may require additional reserved capacity and runbook language — flagging potential uplift.

(attachment: evidence-matrix.xlsx)

Happy to review redlines as they come back.

—Ben

From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@medlinkhealth.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: lortiz@medlinkhealth.com, procurement@medlinkhealth.com
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 15:00:00 -07:00
Subject: MedLink redlines and questions on rider draft

Vivek / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. We reviewed Karthik's draft and Ben's matrix. A few redlines and clarifying asks attached (MedLink_Redlines.docx). Summary:

- We accept Option A but want clarifications in Section 2.1 that availability is measured per-route and excludes customer misconfigurations (we'll provide the SAML metadata).
- We want clarity on credit calculation: please add an example showing a 12h outage and the resulting credit calculation at 99.95 target.
- Evidence access: prefer an API push to our SIEM (Splunk) with hourly payloads for the first 30d; after that, daily summary exports.
- Cross-region failover: MedLink would like an SLA commitment that failover detection and routing will occur within 5m for control-plane leader switch, otherwise a separate credit applies.

We can do a quick call with legal tomorrow if helpful. Also attaching our redlines. DocuSign link will be helpful once we have agreed text.

Thanks,
Samir
(attachment: MedLink_Redlines.docx)

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@medlinkhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 16:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MedLink redlines and questions on rider draft

Samir —

Thanks for the thorough review and the redlines. Next steps and commitments from our side: 

1) We accept Option A as the baseline and will incorporate the clarified per-route measurement language you requested (Section 2.1).
2) Credit calc example: we'll add a worked example for a 12h outage under 99.95 target in Section 3.2 (you'll see the formula and the dollar-equivalent in the order form).
3) Evidence: Redwood can support API push to Splunk for hourly payloads for the first 30d; production cadence will move to daily by default. We'll share the API contract and a sample payload by EOD Wednesday.
4) Cross-region failover: we can commit to routing detection/failover within 5 minutes for control-plane leader changes provided the customer agrees to enable our cross-region routing option (this requires a one-time configuration and modest reserved capacity — we'll detail the uplift). If MedLink declines cross-region routing, fallback to the nearest available region is best-effort and credits would apply only when Redwood's routing fails to meet the stated metric.

I've attached the first pass of the addendum stub (Redwood_SLA_Addendum_v1.docx) and a DocuSign envelope will be prepared once you confirm the legal redlines are addressed. Would you like a 30-min sync tomorrow to walk through the API payload and the credit example?

Best regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(attachment: Redwood_SLA_Addendum_v1.docx)
